title: Representation Alignment for Diffusion Transformers without External Components
claim: Prior methods need an external representation task or pretrained encoder for guidance; ours gets it from the model itself.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right, dashed dividers, (a)/(b)/(c) captions, ours rightmost
description: Three side-by-side block diagrams separated by dashed vertical lines, each captioned (a), (b), (c). Each shows a noisy parrot image feeding a green Diffusion Model box that outputs a Generative Loss arrow upward. Panel (a) adds a red Representation Loss box (e.g., MAE loss) with a Regulation arrow back into the model, plus a mask-grid icon for input processing. Panel (b) adds a yellow Representation Model box (DINOv2) that takes a clean parrot image and produces an Alignment arrow from latent representations. Panel (c), ours, replaces the external model with a blue Diffusion Model linked by a dashed EMA arrow, and the two latent representations feed a Self-Alignment arrow. Colors mark external components versus the self-contained design.
caption: Left: Methods like MaskDiT and SD-DiT use an external representation task to guide diffusion transformer. Middle: Methods like REPA leverage an external representation foundation model as guidance. Right (our approach): We do not use any external representation component but still obtain such guidance through proposed self-representation alignment technique.
abstract: Recent studies have demonstrated that learning a meaningful internal represen- tation can accelerate generative training. However, existing approaches necessi- tate to either introduce an off-the-shelf external representation task or rely on a large-scale, pre-trained external representation encoder to provide representation guidance during the training process. In this study, we posit that the unique dis- criminative process inherent to diffusion transformers enables them to offer such guidance without requiring external representation components. We propose Self- Representation Alignment (SRA), a simple yet effective method that obtains rep- resentation guidance using the internal representations of learned diffusion trans- former. SRA aligns the latent representation of the diffusion transformer in the earlier layer conditioned on higher noise to that in the later layer conditioned on lower noise to progressively enhance the overall representation learning during only the training process. Experimental results indicate that applying SRA to DiTs and SiTs yields consistent performance improvements, and largely outper- forms approaches relying on auxiliary representation task. Our approach achieves performance comparable to methods that are dependent on an external pre-trained representation encoder, which demonstrates the feasibility of acceleration with representation alignment in diffusion transformers themselves.
